symbols.name: N_n
symbols.def: Number of treated donor units at size \(n\).

symbols.name: P_n
symbols.def: Length of the target pre-treatment regression at size \(n\).

symbols.name: M_{m,n}
symbols.def: Number of temporal training columns for mode \(m\in\{\mathrm{dir},\mathrm{rec}\}\).

symbols.name: H_n
symbols.def: Forecast horizon; the growing-path results use \(H_n=\lfloor n^{1/8}\rfloor\), while the comparator embedding sets \(H_n=1\).

symbols.name: \boldsymbol v_n
symbols.def: Alternating vector with entries \(v_{n,j}=(-1)^j\) along the even-index subsequence, so \(\boldsymbol 1_n^{\top}\boldsymbol v_n=0\) and \(\|\boldsymbol v_n\|_2^2=n\).

symbols.name: \varphi
symbols.def: Index of the legal rank-two Gaussian-location submodel.

symbols.name: \mathcal F_n
symbols.def: Sigma-field generated by latent unit factors, latent time factors through lead \(H_n\), assignments, and the deterministic candidate training-cell layout.

symbols.name: \theta_{n,\ell}
symbols.def: Conditional treated mean \(\theta_{n,\ell}=\mathbb E[Y_{0,T+\ell}(1)\mid\mathcal F_n]\) for \(1\le\ell\le H_n\).

symbols.name: \mathcal D_{m,n}
symbols.def: Deterministic menu of admissible temporal training layouts for mode \(m\), with cardinality bounded independently of \(n\).

symbols.name: \widehat d_{m,n}
symbols.def: Measurable empirical-risk minimizer on an auxiliary selection block, with a deterministic tie rule.

symbols.name: \bar Z_{m,n}
symbols.def: Conditional-mean temporal lag design selected by \(\widehat d_{m,n}\).

symbols.name: z_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}
symbols.def: Observed direct temporal response at lead \(\ell\).

symbols.name: \Pi_n
symbols.def: Companion map \(\Pi_n(x)=S_n+e_{L_n}x^{\top}\), where \(S_n\) is the superdiagonal shift.

symbols.name: p_{m,n,\ell}
symbols.def: Unit-side Riesz loading \(p_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}=\bar Y_n^{\dagger\top}\bar W_n a_{n,\ell}\) and \(p_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}=\bar Y_n^{\dagger\top}\bar W_n g_{n,\ell}\).

symbols.name: q_{m,n,\ell}
symbols.def: Temporal Riesz loading \(q_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}=\bar Z_{\mathrm{dir},n}^{\dagger\top}\bar W_n^{\top}\beta_n\) and \(q_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}=\bar Z_{\mathrm{rec},n}^{\dagger\top}J_{n,\ell}^{\top}\bar W_n^{\top}\beta_n\).

symbols.name: G_{m,n,\ell}
symbols.def: Leading orthogonal score at mode \(m\) and lead \(\ell\).

symbols.name: \boldsymbol r_{m,n}
symbols.def: Remainder vector in the selected path linearization.

symbols.name: \widehat Z_{m,n}
symbols.def: Rank-truncated selected temporal design returned by the selected PCR map.

symbols.name: \widehat\beta_n
symbols.def: Selected PCR unit coefficient computed from \((Y_n,y_n)\).

symbols.name: \widehat a_{n,\ell}
symbols.def: Selected direct PCR coefficient computed from \((Z_{\mathrm{dir},n},z_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell})\).

symbols.name: \widehat a_n
symbols.def: Selected recursive PCR coefficient computed from \((Z_{\mathrm{rec},n},z_{\mathrm{rec},n})\).

symbols.name: \widehat J_{n,\ell}
symbols.def: Fitted Jacobian obtained by evaluating the derivative defining \(J_{n,\ell}\) at \(\widehat a_n\).

symbols.name: \widehat p_{m,n,\ell}
symbols.def: Fitted unit-side Riesz loading obtained from the selected rank-truncated unit design and observed \(W_n\).

symbols.name: \widehat q_{m,n,\ell}
symbols.def: Fitted temporal Riesz loading obtained from \(\widehat Z_{m,n}^{\dagger\top}\), observed \(W_n\), \(\widehat\beta_n\), and \(\widehat J_{n,\ell}\) in recursive mode.

symbols.name: \widehat{\boldsymbol\theta}_{m,n}
symbols.def: Selected-training direct or recursive TWSF path center computed by rank-truncated PCR with fitted Riesz corrections that vanish by the fitted normal equations.

symbols.name: \widehat Q_{m,n}
symbols.def: Concatenated fitted coefficient matrix mapping independent primitive cell errors into all \(H_n\) leading score coordinates.

symbols.name: \widehat\Sigma_{m,n}
symbols.def: Observable fitted coefficient-Gram covariance \(\widehat\Sigma_{m,n}=\widehat\sigma_n^2\widehat Q_{m,n}\widehat Q_{m,n}^{\top}\).

symbols.name: \widehat R_{m,n}
symbols.def: Fitted correlation obtained by diagonal normalization of \(\widehat\Sigma_{m,n}\), with the declared measurable fallback on zero fitted variance.

symbols.name: d_{m,n}
symbols.def: Kolmogorov distance between \(\max_{\ell\le H_n}|N(0,\widehat R_{m,n})_\ell|\) conditionally on the data and \(\max_{\ell\le H_n}|N(0,R_{m,n})_\ell|\).

symbols.name: \kappa_{m,n}
symbols.def: Gaussian complexity \(\mathbb E[\max_{\ell\le H_n}|N(0,R_{m,n})_\ell|\mid\mathcal F_n,\widehat d_{m,n}]\).

symbols.name: \nu_{n,\ell}
symbols.def: Lead-specific standardized direct variance share \(\nu_{n,\ell}=\sigma_n^2\|q_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}\|_2^2/s_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}^2\) of the independent lead response.

symbols.name: \rho_n
symbols.def: Heterogeneous-share Gaussian complexity \(\rho_n=\mathbb E[\max_{\ell\le H_n}\sqrt{\nu_{n,\ell}}|\xi_{n,\ell}|]\) for independent \(\xi_{n,\ell}\sim N(0,1)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal C_n
symbols.def: Balanced, strongly identified, fixed-rank TWSF laws satisfying the declared member conditions.

symbols.name: \mathcal A_n
symbols.def: Persistent all-ones rank-one subclass with the declared disjoint common-origin layout.

symbols.name: \mathbb P_{\boldsymbol\vartheta,n}
symbols.def: Member of the explicit rank-two submodel indexed by \(\boldsymbol\vartheta\in\Theta_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal L_n
symbols.def: Gaussian-location family \(\{\mathbb P_{\boldsymbol\vartheta,n}:\boldsymbol\vartheta\in\Theta_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\}\) constructed from constant and alternating factors.

symbols.name: \mathcal S_n^{\mathrm{Shen},1}
symbols.def: The \(H_n=1\) Gaussian, balanced, strongly identified fixed-rank specialization of Shen's published deterministic-training TWSF setup.

symbols.name: \Sigma_n^{\mathrm{loc}}
symbols.def: Covariance of the direct leading score under \(\mathcal L_n\), which does not depend on \(\boldsymbol\vartheta\in\Theta_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\).

symbols.name: X_n
symbols.def: Direct leading Gaussian location observation \(X_n=\boldsymbol\vartheta+\boldsymbol G_{\mathrm{dir},n}\) under \(\mathbb P_{\boldsymbol\vartheta,n}\in\mathcal L_n\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak R_n
symbols.def: Measurable, possibly asymmetric and randomized coordinate rectangles centered at \(X_n\).

symbols.name: W_n^{\max}
symbols.def: Maximum standardized halfwidth of a rectangle in \(\mathfrak R_n\).

symbols.name: \gamma^{\star}
symbols.def: Largest polynomial-horizon exponent derived by the open question \(\mathrm{oeq{:}sharp\mbox{-}horizon}\).

assumptions.condition: Conditional means obey the invariant-unit latent factor model of Shen (2026).
Every treated-state latent temporal component has Hankel rank at most the fixed constant \(Q_0\).
Conditional on \(\mathcal F_n\), the collection of primitive cell errors used in fitting or inference is i.i.d. \(N(0,\sigma_n^2)\).

standard.name: Homoskedastic Gaussian specialization of the TWSF conditional-noise model

assumptions.condition: The common error scale satisfies \(0<c_\sigma\le\sigma_n\le C_\sigma<\infty\).

standard.name: Uniformly bounded and nonvanishing noise scale

assumptions.condition: For fixed \(0<c<C<\infty\), every member satisfies \(cn\le\min\{N_n,P_n,L_n,M_{\mathrm{dir},n},M_{\mathrm{rec},n}\}\le\max\{N_n,P_n,L_n,M_{\mathrm{dir},n},M_{\mathrm{rec},n}\}\le Cn\).
The positive ranks satisfy \(1\le r_{y,n}\vee r_{z,\mathrm{dir},n}\vee r_{z,\mathrm{rec},n}\le r_0\) for a fixed \(r_0\).
Every nonzero singular value of \(\bar Y_n\) and every selectable \(\bar Z_{m,n}\) lies in \([c_s n,C_s n]\).
All entries of the conditional-mean blocks and all conditional target means have absolute value at most a fixed constant \(C_\mu\).
The selected terminal mean satisfies \(\operatorname{col}(\bar W_n)\subseteq\operatorname{col}(\bar Y_n^{\top})\).

standard.name: TWSF unit-side row-span recovery, transposed orientation

assumptions.condition: For every \(1\le\ell\le H_n\) and every selectable direct layout, \(\bar z_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}\in\operatorname{col}(\bar Z_{\mathrm{dir},n})\).

novel.justification: This uniform selected-layout version of Shen's fixed-summary span condition is satisfied when each deterministic candidate Page block spans the same finite recurrence space, as for persistent harmonic, polynomial, and exponential factor sequences.

assumptions.condition: For every \(1\le\ell\le H_n\), the coefficient \(a_{n,\ell}\) represents the terminal-state conditional mean through \(\theta_{n,\ell}=a_{n,\ell}^{\top}\bar W_n^{\top}\beta_n\).

novel.justification: A common-origin terminal block generated by a finite recurrence has the same horizon-specific coefficient as any correctly aligned training response; persistent and harmonic factor paths provide concrete examples.

assumptions.condition: For every selectable recursive layout and every \(0\le j<H_n\), each population terminal state advanced \(j\) times by a valid population recurrence belongs to \(\operatorname{col}(\bar Z_{\mathrm{rec},n})\).

novel.justification: This is a selected-layout strengthening of Shen's recursive recovery condition. It is satisfied by persistent harmonic, polynomial, and exponential factor sequences when each deterministic candidate Page block spans the common recurrence space, and it can be screened by predeclared span diagnostics.

assumptions.condition: The auxiliary errors determining \(\widehat d_{m,n}\) are independent, conditional on \(\mathcal F_n\), of all errors in \(Y_n,y_n,Z_{m,n},z_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell},z_{\mathrm{rec},n},W_n\).

novel.justification: A held-out validation segment is available in prospective panels before the terminal forecast origin, so training layout can be selected on cells excluded from the final fit and Gram calculation. The condition accommodates exact and local risk ties because the tie rule is fixed and measurable.

assumptions.condition: Within a mode, pre-treatment, lag-design, temporal-response, terminal-history, and auxiliary-selection cells are pairwise disjoint whenever their independence is invoked.
For a fixed \(c_v>0\), \(\min_{m\in\{\mathrm{dir},\mathrm{rec}\},\ell\le H_n}s_{m,n,\ell}\ge c_vn^{-1/2}\).

standard.name: Uniform marginal-variance nondegeneracy without an eigenvalue bound

assumptions.condition: For a fixed \(C_A\), \(\max_{0\le j\le H_n}\|\Pi_n(a_n)^j\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C_A\) uniformly over selectable recursive layouts.

novel.justification: Short-horizon power boundedness holds for stable and unit-root recurrences with semisimple unit roots, including constant, polynomial-trend after state augmentation, and finite-harmonic factor paths used in economic panels.

assumptions.condition: Every donor and target loading equals one.

novel.justification: A common level loading represents panels whose units share one persistent aggregate factor while retaining nondegenerate idiosyncratic cell noise.

assumptions.condition: Every relevant treated and control mean time factor equals one.

novel.justification: A persistent level factor is a standard component of epidemic counts, demand, and macroeconomic panels, and yields strongly identified rank-one blocks rather than a collapsed signal.

assumptions.condition: On the persistent subclass, \(N_n=P_n=L_n=M_{\mathrm{dir},n}=M_{\mathrm{rec},n}=n\).

novel.justification: Equal block lengths give an implementable balanced benchmark with all signal singular values proportional to \(n\).

assumptions.condition: On the persistent subclass, \(|\mathcal D_{\mathrm{dir},n}|=|\mathcal D_{\mathrm{rec},n}|=1\).

novel.justification: A singleton menu is the deterministic-training special case used to isolate architecture rather than selection complexity.

assumptions.condition: The persistent direct and recursive layouts use the same terminal block \(W_n\) and the same forecast origin.

novel.justification: Reserving one terminal donor-history block at a common decision date is feasible in prospective panels and makes the architecture comparison hold the forecasting target fixed.

definitions.name: Selected PCR map
definitions.construction: For each observed design \(X\), retain the declared rank singular subspace, set \(X_r=\operatorname{HSVT}(X,r)\), and return \(X_r^\dagger u\) for response \(u\); use the threshold \(n_*^{3/4}\) and a deterministic spectral-tie convention when ranks are not supplied.

definitions.name: \(\boldsymbol G_{m,n}\)
definitions.construction: Let \(\delta_{\beta,n}=e_{y,n}-E_{Y,n}\beta_n\), \(\delta_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}=e_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}-E_{Z,\mathrm{dir},n}a_{n,\ell}\), and \(\delta_{\mathrm{rec},n}=e_{\mathrm{rec},n}-E_{Z,\mathrm{rec},n}a_n\). Define \(G_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}=a_{n,\ell}^{\top}E_{W,n}^{\top}\beta_n+p_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}^{\top}\delta_{\beta,n}+q_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}^{\top}\delta_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}\) and \(G_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}=g_{n,\ell}^{\top}E_{W,n}^{\top}\beta_n+p_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}^{\top}\delta_{\beta,n}+q_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}^{\top}\delta_{\mathrm{rec},n}\), then stack over \(1\le\ell\le H_n\).

definitions.name: \(\widehat\Sigma_{m,n}\)
definitions.construction: Write each fitted score coordinate as a concatenated coefficient vector multiplying the independent Gaussian primitive blocks, and set \(\widehat\Sigma_{m,n}=\widehat\sigma_n^2\widehat Q_{m,n}\widehat Q_{m,n}^{\top}\), where \(\widehat Q_{m,n}\) uses the selected rank-truncated PCR coefficients, observed \(W_n\), fitted Riesz vectors, and fitted companion Jacobians. Estimate \(\sigma_n^2\) by the pooled unit-response and first temporal-response residual sum of squares divided by their residual degrees of freedom.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal B_{m,n}\)
definitions.construction: Simulate \(Z^{\ast}_{m,n}\mid\mathrm{data}\sim N(0,\widehat R_{m,n})\), take \(\widehat c_{m,n}(1-\alpha)=\inf\{c:\Pr(\max_{\ell\le H_n}|Z^{\ast}_{m,n,\ell}|\le c\mid\mathrm{data})\ge1-\alpha\}\), and form \(\mathcal B_{m,n}=\prod_{\ell=1}^{H_n}[\widehat\theta_{m,n,\ell}\pm\widehat c_{m,n}(1-\alpha)\widehat s_{m,n,\ell}]\), with a deterministic measurable fallback on spectral or variance failure.

definitions.name: Variance-share Gaussian-complexity frontier
definitions.construction:
The focal map is \((R_{\mathrm{dir},n},R_{\mathrm{rec},n})\mapsto((
u_{n,\ell})_{\ell=1}^{H_n},ho_n,\kappa_{\mathrm{dir},n},\kappa_{\mathrm{rec},n})\), where \(
u_{n,\ell}=\sigma_n^2\|q_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}\|_2^2/s_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}^2\), \(ho_n=\mathbb E\max_{\ell\le H_n}\sqrt{
u_{n,\ell}}|\xi_{n,\ell}|\) for independent standard normal \(\xi_{n,\ell}\), and \(\kappa_{m,n}=\mathbb E\max_{\ell\le H_n}|N(0,R_{m,n})_\ell|\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal L_n\)
definitions.construction: Along even \(n\), let \(\boldsymbol u_n=\boldsymbol 1_n\), \(B_n=\boldsymbol u_n\boldsymbol u_n^{\top}+\boldsymbol v_n\boldsymbol v_n^{\top}\), and use mutually disjoint observed blocks with \(N_n=P_n=L_n=M_{\mathrm{dir},n}=M_{\mathrm{rec},n}=n\), singleton training menus, \(\bar Y_n=\bar Z_{\mathrm{dir},n}=\bar Z_{\mathrm{rec},n}=\bar W_n=B_n\), \(\bar y_n(\varphi)=\cos(\varphi)\boldsymbol u_n+\sin(\varphi)\boldsymbol v_n\), \(\bar z_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}=\boldsymbol u_n+(-1)^\ell\boldsymbol v_n\), \(\bar z_{\mathrm{rec},n}=\boldsymbol u_n-\boldsymbol v_n\), and i.i.d. \(N(0,\sigma_n^2)\) cell errors. Constant and alternating latent factors generate these blocks and give \(\boldsymbol\theta_n=\boldsymbol\vartheta_n(\varphi)=\cos(\varphi)\boldsymbol 1_{H_n}+\sin(\varphi)\boldsymbol h_n\). The resulting indexed family is \(\mathcal L_n=\{\mathbb P_{\boldsymbol\vartheta,n}:\boldsymbol\vartheta\in\Theta_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal S_n^{\mathrm{Shen},1}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal S_n^{\mathrm{Shen},1}=\{P:P\text{ is in Shen's published deterministic-training TWSF setup with }H_n=1,\ |\mathcal D_{\mathrm{dir},n}|=|\mathcal D_{\mathrm{rec},n}|=1,\text{ and satisfies }\mathrm{ass{:}factor\mbox{-}model},\mathrm{ass{:}hankel\mbox{-}rank},\mathrm{ass{:}gaussian\mbox{-}cells},\mathrm{ass{:}noise\mbox{-}scale},\mathrm{ass{:}balanced\mbox{-}dimensions},\mathrm{ass{:}fixed\mbox{-}rank},\mathrm{ass{:}strong\mbox{-}spectrum},\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\mbox{-}means},\mathrm{ass{:}unit\mbox{-}recovery},\mathrm{ass{:}direct\mbox{-}response\mbox{-}span},\mathrm{ass{:}direct\mbox{-}terminal\mbox{-}transport},\mathrm{ass{:}recursive\mbox{-}recovery},\mathrm{ass{:}independent\mbox{-}selection},\mathrm{ass{:}disjoint\mbox{-}inference\mbox{-}blocks},\mathrm{ass{:}variance\mbox{-}floor},\mathrm{ass{:}stable\mbox{-}short\mbox{-}recursion}\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak R_n\)
definitions.construction: In the experiment \(X_n\mid\mathbb P_{\boldsymbol\vartheta,n}\sim N(\boldsymbol\vartheta,\Sigma_n^{\mathrm{loc}})\), define \(\mathfrak R_n=\{\prod_{\ell=1}^{H_n}[X_{n,\ell}-s_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}W^-_{n,\ell},X_{n,\ell}+s_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}W^+_{n,\ell}]:W^-_{n,\ell},W^+_{n,\ell}\ge0\text{ are measurable in }(X_n,U)\}\), where \(U\) is independent auxiliary randomization, \(\Sigma_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\) is the direct leading-score covariance common to every \(\boldsymbol\vartheta\in\Theta_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\), and \(W_n^{\max}=\max_{\ell\le H_n}(W^-_{n,\ell}\vee W^+_{n,\ell})\).

definitions.name: Sharp-horizon audit handle
definitions.construction: Use the exact sixteen-term orthogonal remainder ledger, a leave-one-block-out spectral coupling for the implemented PCR map, and second-order Fr\'{e}chet bounds for \(x\mapsto\Pi_n(x)^\ell\) to determine \(\gamma^{\star}\) and a matching legal failure sequence.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal C_n\) and conditionally on \((\mathcal F_n,\widehat d_{m,n})\), the selected direct and recursive centers satisfy \(\widehat{\boldsymbol\theta}_{m,n}-\boldsymbol\theta_n=\boldsymbol G_{m,n}+\boldsymbol r_{m,n}\), where \(\boldsymbol G_{m,n}\) is exactly Gaussian with covariance \(\Sigma_{m,n}\), \(\max_{\ell\le H_n}|r_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}|/s_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}=O_{\Pr}(\log(nH_n)/\sqrt n)\), and \(\max_{\ell\le H_n}|r_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}|/s_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}=O_{\Pr}(H_n\log(nH_n)/\sqrt n+H_n^2\log(nH_n)/n)\). The direct and recursive score coordinates equal the constructions in \(\mathrm{def{:}stacked\mbox{-}scores}\).
statements.justification: This is the panel-specific uniform linearization that turns a displayed path into one inferential object.
statements.gap: Shen (2026, Appendices S12--S13) proves scalar fixed-summary expansions; stacking before aggregation and tracking every power of \(H_n\) is new.
statements.consumer: It supplies the influence-score path required for an honest simultaneous conditional-mean ribbon in the TWSF component of \(\texttt{mlsynth}\).

statements.statement: The construction \(\widehat\Sigma_{m,n}\) is observable and positive semidefinite. Uniformly over \(\mathcal C_n\), \(\max_{\ell,k\le H_n}|\widehat\Sigma_{\mathrm{dir},n}(\ell,k)-\Sigma_{\mathrm{dir},n}(\ell,k)|/(s_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}s_{\mathrm{dir},n,k})=O_{\Pr}(\sqrt{\log(nH_n)/n})\) and the recursive analogue is \(O_{\Pr}(H_n^2\sqrt{\log(nH_n)/n})\). On the same event, \(t_{m,n}\lesssim\Delta_{m,n}\lesssim\max_{\ell,k}|\widehat\Sigma_{m,n}(\ell,k)-\Sigma_{m,n}(\ell,k)|/(s_{m,n,\ell}s_{m,n,k})\).
statements.justification: Relative rather than raw covariance accuracy is the last feasible-input condition for a singular multiplier path law.
statements.gap: Agarwal, Shah, and Shen (2025) control PCR prediction directions, and Shen (2026) controls a scalar variance; neither controls the actual fitted cross-lead Gram matrix after recursive Jacobian propagation.
statements.consumer: The result provides a software-computable covariance matrix without latent factors, oracle terminal blocks, or covariance inversion.

statements.statement: If \((\kappa_{m,n}+1)\varepsilon_{m,n}+(\kappa_{m,n}+1)^2t_{m,n}+d_{m,n}=o_{\Pr}(1)\) uniformly over \(\mathcal C_n\), then \(\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal C_n}|\Pr_{\mathbb P}(\boldsymbol\theta_n\in\mathcal B_{m,n}\mid\mathcal F_n)-(1-\alpha)|\to0\) for each prespecified mode \(m\in\{\mathrm{dir},\mathrm{rec}\}\), with no lower eigenvalue condition on \(R_{m,n}\). The rates in Theorems \(\mathrm{thm{:}stacked\mbox{-}orthogonal\mbox{-}expansion}\) and \(\mathrm{thm{:}relative\mbox{-}gram\mbox{-}rate}\), together with Gaussian comparison, verify the premise at \(H_n=\lfloor n^{1/8}\rfloor\). This strictly strengthens Shen's fixed-summary pointwise interval within the declared selected-training class by covering all \(H_n\) conditional means jointly.
statements.justification: This is the headline feasible simultaneous-coverage result and explicitly accounts for remainder, studentization, and multiplier-law errors.
statements.gap: Shen (2026, Corollary 2 and Section 6) gives pointwise inference for prespecified fixed-horizon summaries, while Belloni et al. (2018) does not derive the TWSF score and covariance inputs. Greenaway-McGrevy (2013) compares direct and recursive panel-VAR forecasts by asymptotic MSPE, but does not construct a causal selected-training score, a feasible cross-lead Gram covariance, or a simultaneous conditional-mean ribbon.
statements.consumer: It turns the daily conditional-mean forecasts used in Shen's NFL-stadium analysis into one jointly interpretable path ribbon; cumulative paths require a separately transformed covariance audit.

statements.justification: The theorem identifies the heterogeneous independent-share complexity that determines the multiplicity cost of separate direct temporal rules.
statements.gap: Greenaway-McGrevy (2013) is the nearest direct-versus-recursive panel forecasting comparator: it derives asymptotic MSPE expressions for conventional recursive and direct panel-VAR forecasts and ranks them under correct, over-, and under-specified lag orders. An MSPE ranking does not imply the causal TWSF Gaussian-maximum or variance-share frontier stated here; Shen (2026) remains the exact causal-forecasting anchor, while Chernozhukov et al. (2015) supplies only generic Gaussian comparison tools once covariance is known.
statements.consumer: The result tells a practitioner when direct TWSF ribbons must widen with horizon and when recursive ribbons retain a constant critical-value scale.

For \(H_n=\lfloor n^{1/8}floor\), the constructed subclass \(\mathcal A_n\) is nonempty and satisfies \(\mathcal A_n\subset\mathcal C_n\). On \(\mathcal A_n\), \( eta_n= oldsymbol 1/n\), \(a_n=a_{n,\ell}= oldsymbol 1/n\), \(J_{n,\ell}^{	op} oldsymbol 1=c_{n,\ell} oldsymbol 1\) with \(c_{n,\ell}=(1+1/n)^{\ell-1}\), \(\|g_{n,\ell}\|_2^2=n^{-1}+O(H_n/n^2)\), and \(
u_{n,\ell}=
u_{\min,n}=
u_{\max,n}=1/(2+3/n)\) for every lead. Consequently, \(\kappa_{\mathrm{rec},n}	o\sqrt{2/\pi}\) and \(\kappa_{\mathrm{dir},n}/\sqrt{\log H_n}	o1\); the corresponding fixed-level Gaussian maximum quantiles have limits \(\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\) and \(1\) after division by \(\sqrt{\log H_n}\), respectively.
statements.justification: The exact subclass proves that the complexity separation is attainable within the legal fixed-rank model rather than being an abstract covariance example.
statements.gap: No located TWSF result computes the full five-component variance shares or the direct and recursive Gaussian maximum limits on a persistent common-origin sequence.
statements.consumer: The limit gives an interpretable benchmark for the critical values produced by a TWSF ribbon implementation.

statements.statement: For \(H_n=\lfloor n^{1/8}\rfloor\) along even \(n\), the constructed family is nondegenerate and satisfies \(\mathcal L_n=\{\mathbb P_{\boldsymbol\vartheta,n}:\boldsymbol\vartheta\in\Theta_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\}\subset\mathcal C_n\). Under every \(\mathbb P_{\boldsymbol\vartheta,n}\), \(X_n\sim N(\boldsymbol\vartheta,\Sigma_n^{\mathrm{loc}})\) conditionally on \(\mathcal F_n\), where \(\Sigma_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\) is independent of \(\boldsymbol\vartheta\), \(s_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}^2=\sigma_n^2(3/n+6/n^2)\), and the independent direct lead-response share equals \((3+6/n)^{-1}\) for every \(\ell\le H_n\).
statements.justification: This proposition supplies the legal fixed-covariance location experiment required by the centered-width argument.
statements.gap: The persistent rank-one calculation fixes its mean path and therefore cannot itself support an honesty infimum over a nondegenerate location parameter.
statements.consumer: It makes the direct-width certificate auditable as a restriction of the declared TWSF class rather than as an external Gaussian comparison experiment.

statements.statement: Along the even-index sequence in \(\mathcal L_n\), fix \(0<\eta<1\). For any sequence of rectangles \(C_n^{\mathrm{rect}}\in\mathfrak R_n\) satisfying \(\inf_{\boldsymbol\vartheta\in\Theta_n^{\mathrm{loc}}}\Pr_{\mathbb P_{\boldsymbol\vartheta,n}}(\boldsymbol\vartheta\in C_n^{\mathrm{rect}}\mid\mathcal F_n)\ge1-\alpha-\delta_n\) with \(\delta_n\to0\), \(\inf_{\boldsymbol\vartheta\in\Theta_n^{\mathrm{loc}}}\Pr_{\mathbb P_{\boldsymbol\vartheta,n}}\{W_n^{\max}\ge(1-\eta)\sqrt{2(3+6/n)^{-1}\log H_n}\mid\mathcal F_n\}\ge1-\alpha-\delta_n-o(1)\) and \(\inf_{\boldsymbol\vartheta\in\Theta_n^{\mathrm{loc}}}\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{\boldsymbol\vartheta,n}}[W_n^{\max}\mid\mathcal F_n]\ge(1-\eta)\sqrt{2(3+6/n)^{-1}\log H_n}\{1-\alpha-\delta_n-o(1)\}\). The quantifiers include asymmetric, data-dependent, and randomized widths centered at \(X_n\), but not alternative centers or unrestricted estimators.
statements.justification: The result certifies that the direct multiplicity cost cannot be hidden by randomized or adaptive widths around the stated center.
statements.gap: Cai, Low, and Ma (2014) prove width limits for nonparametric function classes, not for this legal rank-two TWSF Gaussian-location submodel or this estimator-centered scope.
statements.consumer: It prevents a direct-TWSF implementation from advertising pointwise-width ribbons as uniformly honest through data-dependent horizonwise resizing.

statements.statement: The identity embedding of observed blocks, target, and deterministic training layout satisfies \(\mathcal S_n^{\mathrm{Shen},1}\subset\{\mathbb P\in\mathcal C_n:H_n=1,\ |\mathcal D_{\mathrm{dir},n}|=|\mathcal D_{\mathrm{rec},n}|=1\}\). On this embedded class, selection is deterministic, \(\widehat c_{m,n}(1-\alpha)=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)+o_{\Pr}(1)\), and Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}selected\mbox{-}band}\) recovers Shen's published pointwise TWSF interval under the declared Gaussian specialization.
statements.justification: This explicit singleton-menu inclusion anchors the growing-path result to the published one-coordinate setup.
statements.gap: The recovered pointwise interval is prior-art validation and is not claimed as a new contribution.
statements.consumer: It ensures backward compatibility with existing pointwise TWSF reporting.

statements.statement: Determine the largest \(\gamma^{\star}\) such that, for every \(\gamma<\gamma^{\star}\) and \(H_n\le n^\gamma\), the actual selected-PCR recursive construction satisfies \((\kappa_{\mathrm{rec},n}+1)\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rec},n}+(\kappa_{\mathrm{rec},n}+1)^2t_{\mathrm{rec},n}+d_{\mathrm{rec},n}=o_{\Pr}(1)\) uniformly over \(\mathcal C_n\), and construct a legal sequence in \(\mathcal C_n\) on which at least one term fails to vanish for every \(\gamma>\gamma^{\star}\).
statements.justification: The sufficient exponent \(1/8\) is useful but may reflect conservative companion and Gram perturbation bounds; the sharp horizon-information boundary is genuinely unresolved.
statements.gap: Shen (2026) holds the horizon fixed, and no adjacent PCR or Gaussian-comparison paper determines a maximal growing TWSF horizon for the implemented estimator.
statements.consumer: A sharp exponent would determine how far a software ribbon may extrapolate as panel size grows and would separate estimator limitations from proof slack.

sampling_model.design: Balanced fixed-rank latent-factor panel with deterministic candidate Page blocks, one common terminal block and forecast origin, and auxiliary-block empirical-risk selection with deterministic tie breaking.
sampling_model.units: One untreated target and \(N_n\) treated donors, conditioned on latent unit and time factors and assignments through lead \(H_n\).
sampling_model.treatment: Donors reveal treated post-period trajectories; the target remains untreated in the observed panel, and the target is its prospective treated conditional-mean path.
sampling_model.overlap: Unit-side and selected temporal row-span recovery hold for every candidate layout; path covariance may be singular, but each marginal leading variance is at least \(c_v^2/n\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Rank-truncated PCR estimates unit and temporal coefficients; fitted Riesz vectors, the observed terminal block, recursive Jacobians, and a pooled residual variance form the observable positive-semidefinite Gram covariance.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper establishes pointwise identification, finite-sample error bounds, consistency, asymptotic normality, and inference for prespecified linear summaries over fixed forecast horizons.
The paper derives asymptotic MSPE expressions for conventional recursive and direct multistep panel-VAR forecasts and shows that their ranking changes with lag-order specification.
The paper derives asymptotic distributions and MSPE comparisons for direct and plug-in multistep predictors in finite-order autoregressive time series.
The paper obtains asymptotic MSPE expressions for plug-in and direct multistep predictors in autoregressive processes and compares their performance in stationary and deterministic-trend settings.
The procedure constructs simultaneous confidence bands for many functional parameters using approximately Neyman-orthogonal scores.
The paper gives comparison and anti-concentration bounds for maxima with arbitrary covariance matrices.
The paper derives Gaussian and bootstrap approximations uniformly over high-dimensional hyperrectangles.
The paper establishes nonasymptotic out-of-sample prediction guarantees for fixed-design principal component regression with errors in variables.
The paper establishes asymptotic normality for low-rank completion without requiring implemented sample splitting.
The paper proves residual-bootstrap intervals for individual treated unit-time effects in an interactive-fixed-effects panel.
The paper derives expected-width lower bounds for honest random confidence bands over nonparametric regression classes.

tldr: A selected-training Two-Way Synthetic Forecasting path is treated as one growing, conditionally Gaussian orthogonal-score object rather than as a collection of pointwise forecasts. On a balanced strongly identified fixed-rank panel class, the paper derives the joint direct and recursive scores, constructs observable positive-semidefinite Gram covariance estimators from the fitted PCR, Riesz, terminal-block, and recursive-Jacobian objects, and proves feasible multiplier coverage for \(H_n=\lfloor n^{1/8}\rfloor\). The covariance decomposition yields a heterogeneous variance-share frontier: recursive Gaussian complexity is uniformly bounded, whereas direct complexity is comparable to \(1+\rho_n\), the expected maximum of independent normals scaled by their lead-specific direct shares. This complexity and simultaneous-inference comparison is distinct from the direct-versus-recursive panel-VAR MSPE ranking of Greenaway-McGrevy (2013). A persistent rank-one subclass gives the exact limits \(\kappa_{\mathrm{rec},n}\to\sqrt{2/\pi}\) and \(\kappa_{\mathrm{dir},n}/\sqrt{\log H_n}\to1\); a separate explicit rank-two TWSF Gaussian-location submodel yields probability and expected maximum-width lower bounds for uniformly honest rectangles centered at the direct leading Gaussian estimator. An \(H_n=1\) singleton-menu inclusion recovers Shen's pointwise setup solely as prior-art validation.

project_justification.gap: Shen (2026, Corollary 2 and Section 6) establishes pointwise inference for prespecified fixed-horizon summaries, not a growing selected path. Greenaway-McGrevy (2013) derives asymptotic MSPE expressions for conventional direct and recursive panel-VAR forecasts, but an MSPE ranking does not provide a causal TWSF selected-training score, a Gaussian maximum or variance-share frontier, a feasible cross-lead Gram covariance, or a simultaneous conditional-mean ribbon. Generic orthogonal-score and Gaussian-comparison results begin after uniform linearization and covariance control have been supplied.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is an observable joint law for direct and recursive causal conditional-mean paths that remains valid under singular correlation and exposes how a heterogeneous vector of lead-specific innovations alters the critical-value scale, a criterion orthogonal to forecast MSPE ranking.
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies the stacked causal TWSF score and positive-semidefinite Gram map, proves the actual-estimator relative covariance and simultaneous-coverage rates at \(H_n=\lfloor n^{1/8}\rfloor\), characterizes direct complexity through the aggregate heterogeneous-share quantity \(\rho_n\), and certifies the architectural separation on a persistent rank-one subclass. It places the centered-rectangle width cost on an explicit legal rank-two Gaussian-location submodel and embeds Shen's published pointwise setup at \(H_n=1\) with singleton training menus; it makes no claim to sharpen Greenaway-McGrevy's panel-VAR MSPE ranking.

related_work: Shen (2026) is the exact causal-forecasting anchor: Theorem 1 identifies the prospective treated conditional mean, Corollary 2 gives pointwise inference, and Section 6 treats prespecified direct and recursive summaries over fixed horizons. The explicit \(H_n=1\) singleton-menu inclusion recovers that pointwise interval as a validation check, not as novelty; the selected growing-path theorem strictly tightens the published fixed-summary result by covering all \(H_n\) conditional means jointly. Greenaway-McGrevy (2013) is the nearest direct-versus-recursive architecture comparator in panel forecasting: the paper derives asymptotic MSPE expressions for conventional recursive, or plug-in, and direct multistep forecasts in a panel vector autoregression, with the ranking governed by lag-order specification. That MSPE comparison informs the architectural motivation but does not supply the causal TWSF selected-training score construction, Gaussian maximum or variance-share complexity frontier, feasible Gram covariance, or simultaneous conditional-mean ribbon. Bhansali (1997) provides the earlier time-series comparison of direct and plug-in autoregressive predictors through asymptotic distributions, MSPE, and efficiency loss, not a panel causal path law. Ing (2003) likewise compares plug-in and direct multistep predictors by asymptotic MSPE in autoregressive processes, including deterministic-trend cases, without addressing selected low-rank panel inference. Belloni, Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Wei (2018) inform the use of uniform orthogonal expansions and multiplier critical values but do not derive the low-rank panel scores. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2015, 2017) inform comparison, anti-concentration, and singular-covariance hyperrectangle approximation; they are probability inputs rather than theorem-level targets. Agarwal, Shah, and Shen (2025) inform the fixed-design PCR perturbation step, while Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2024) inform the proof-only decoupling of factor estimation from target noise. Li, Shen, and Zhou (2024) provide the nearest residual-bootstrap panel inference, but their object is an individual treated unit-time effect rather than a prospective growing path. Cai, Low, and Ma (2014) inform random-band width arguments; the present lower result is confined to rectangles centered at the direct leading Gaussian estimator in the explicit legal family \(\mathcal L_n\).
technical_internal_limitation: The first kill test is the actual-estimator three-piece perturbation \(\widehat q_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}-q_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}=(\widehat Z^\dagger-\bar Z^\dagger)J_{n,\ell}^{\top}w_n+\widehat Z^\dagger J_{n,\ell}^{\top}(W_n^{\top}\widehat\beta_n-w_n)+\widehat Z^\dagger(\widehat J_{n,\ell}-J_{n,\ell})^{\top}W_n^{\top}\widehat\beta_n\). The proposal fails if an independent audit finds an order-one studentized term, an invalid projector-response independence step, or a need to replace observed \(W_n\) or fitted \(J_{n,\ell}\) by oracle objects. The rank-two location construction also requires a cell-index audit showing that the constant and alternating factors realize every displayed block with disjoint cells and a power-bounded two-root recurrence. Explicit constants, measurable exceptional-event endpoints, finite multiplier-simulation error, and software integration remain proof and implementation tasks rather than additional assumptions.
honest_scope: The proved target is the prospective treated conditional-mean path, not realized-future prediction. Training-layout selection must use the declared auxiliary block; arbitrary reuse of inference cells and data-driven selection between direct and recursive modes are excluded. The result assumes independent homoskedastic Gaussian cell errors, fixed rank, strong spectral identification, and the sufficient growing horizon \(H_n=\lfloor n^{1/8}\rfloor\). The exact recursive and direct complexity limits hold on the persistent all-ones subclass, while the heterogeneous-share order comparison holds over \(\mathcal C_n\); a minimum-share-only upper law is asserted only under uniform share comparability. The width lower bound uses the nondegenerate legal rank-two family \(\mathcal L_n\), concerns rectangles centered at its direct leading Gaussian estimator, and makes no unrestricted-estimator minimax claim. The \(H_n=1\) singleton-menu result is only a prior-art reduction. The sharp maximal growing horizon is left as the explicit open-ended question.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, Theorem 1, Corollary 2, Section 6, Appendices S12--S13, and the Conclusion were read in arXiv version 3.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Appendix S12 collapses a fixed direct summary to one regression and Appendix S13 propagates one fixed recursive summary; the first changed step is to retain every lead before aggregation and control the selected \(H_n\)-vector and its fitted covariance jointly.
seed_details.destination_search: The pair \(\{\text{selected TWSF path},\text{multiplier hyperrectangle}\}\) was searched against Belloni et al. (2018), Chernozhukov et al. (2017), Li et al. (2024), and Choi et al. (2024); none contains the TWSF-specific growing-path construction.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Belloni et al. (2018) after calling each lead an orthogonal target.
seed_details.rebuttal: That theorem assumes a controlled score family; here the leading score, observable covariance, selection map, and uniform PCR/Jacobian remainders must first be derived from one reused noisy panel, including singular correlation.
seed_details.key_inspiration: Adapt the uniform Bahadur-to-multiplier arc of Belloni et al. (2018), but replace empirical score covariance by a coefficient-based positive-semidefinite Gram map whose perturbation is proved for the actual fitted TWSF objects.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Section 6.3 and Appendices S12--S13 were read; they compare direct and recursive pointwise constructions without analyzing their joint Gaussian maxima.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed proof step is to keep the common-score subspace and the independent direct response contribution separate after standardization, rather than reducing the horizon to a fixed scalar summary.
seed_details.destination_search: The pair \(\{\text{TWSF covariance geometry},\text{Gaussian maximum complexity}\}\) was checked against Chernozhukov et al. (2013, 2015, 2017) and Greenaway-McGrevy (2013). The probability papers do not derive a panel-structural frontier, while Greenaway-McGrevy compares direct and recursive panel-VAR forecasts through asymptotic MSPE rather than Gaussian maximum complexity or simultaneous inference.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from the standard bound \(\mathbb E\max_{\ell\le H}|Z_\ell|\asymp\sqrt{\log H}\).
seed_details.rebuttal: The work is to derive the decomposition with a fixed-dimensional common component and the heterogeneous independent-share complexity \(\rho_n\) from TWSF scores and to prove bounded recursion on the full declared class; generic maximum bounds do not supply either structural fact.
seed_details.key_inspiration: Use arbitrary-covariance comparison only after an exact TWSF score decomposition isolates lead-specific direct innovations from a common fixed-rank Gaussian subspace.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The pointwise interval in Corollary 2 and the conditional-mean NFL path in Section 8.2.2 were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to embed a nondegenerate rank-two constant-and-alternating-factor family in the declared TWSF class, prove that its direct leading covariance is invariant to the indexed mean path, and then turn simultaneous honesty into a maximum event before allowing data-dependent, asymmetric, or randomized coordinate widths.
seed_details.destination_search: The pair \(\{\text{TWSF-centered rectangles},\text{random maximum-width lower bound}\}\) was checked against Cai et al. (2014), Chernozhukov et al. (2014), and Armstrong and Koles\'{a}r (2018); those results concern different function classes or decision geometries.
seed_details.red_team: A trivial consequence of Gaussian quantiles and therefore not a research result.
seed_details.rebuttal: The nontrivial content is the legal TWSF embedding with exact independent variance share and the uniform quantifiers over data-dependent and randomized widths; the claim is deliberately restricted to the direct leading-Gaussian center.
seed_details.key_inspiration: Borrow honesty-to-testing logic from Cai et al. (2014), but apply it to the explicit legal rank-two TWSF Gaussian-location family rather than to an external comparison experiment.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, Theorems 4.1--4.2, Section 4.3, and the Conclusion were read in the JMLR paper.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to perturb an entire cross-lead Gram matrix after multiplying PCR directions by fitted Riesz maps, noisy terminal histories, and companion Jacobians.
seed_details.destination_search: No paper located for \(\{\text{actual TWSF PCR},\text{relative max-norm covariance}\}\).
seed_details.red_team: A routine polarization of existing PCR prediction bounds.
seed_details.rebuttal: Prediction error does not control studentized pairwise Gram entries when the marginal variances are of order \(n^{-1}\) and the recursive direction contains an estimated Jacobian and noisy terminal block.

literature_map.settled: Shen (2026, Theorem 1) identifies the prospective conditional mean and Corollary 2 gives feasible pointwise inference; Section 6 treats prespecified summaries over fixed horizons through direct and recursive PCR.
literature_map.open_boundary: No theorem there gives a simultaneous band for all coordinates of a growing path, a post-training-selection map, or a cross-lead covariance estimator.

literature_map.thread: Direct versus recursive multistep panel forecasting
literature_map.settled: Bhansali (1997) and Ing (2003) derive asymptotic distributions or MSPE expressions comparing direct and plug-in multistep predictors in autoregressive time series. Greenaway-McGrevy (2013, abstract and main-result summary) carries the comparison to panel vector autoregressions: direct MSPE is larger when the fitted lag order is at least the true order, while direct MSPE is smaller under lag-order underspecification.
literature_map.open_boundary: These MSPE rankings concern predictive accuracy in autoregressive models; they do not derive a causal TWSF selected-training score, a Gaussian maximum or variance-share complexity frontier, an observable cross-lead Gram covariance, or a simultaneous conditional-mean ribbon.

literature_map.settled: Belloni et al. (2018, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2) transfer a uniform Bahadur representation to multiplier confidence regions for many approximately orthogonal targets.
literature_map.open_boundary: The score family and its covariance are inputs to that framework; the paper does not derive them from reused noisy low-rank panel regressions or recursive companion derivatives.

literature_map.settled: Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2015, Theorems 2--3) give covariance-comparison and anti-concentration bounds for arbitrary Gaussian covariance, and their 2017 paper gives hyperrectangle Gaussian and bootstrap approximation.
literature_map.open_boundary: These probability tools do not identify the TWSF covariance geometry, its heterogeneous-share aggregate \(\rho_n\), or the actual-PCR relative covariance rate.

literature_map.settled: Arkhangelsky and Imbens (2024) survey modern longitudinal and panel causal models and identify dynamics and time-series structure as a continuing divide; Li, Shen, and Zhou (2024) give residual-bootstrap intervals for individual treated cells, while Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2024) use an auxiliary leave-one-out proof to obtain entrywise low-rank inference without implementing sample splitting.
literature_map.open_boundary: The survey and the two inference papers do not treat a prospective recursive path, selected TWSF training, or a growing singular score Gram matrix.

literature_map.settled: Agarwal, Shah, and Shen (2025) establish minimum-norm identification and nonasymptotic out-of-sample prediction guarantees for fixed-design PCR.
literature_map.open_boundary: Directionwise prediction bounds do not yield studentized cross-lead covariance control after fitted Riesz, terminal-block, and Jacobian transformations.

literature_map.settled: Cai, Low, and Ma (2014) derive random-band width limits for nonparametric regression classes.
literature_map.open_boundary: Their nonparametric smoothness experiment does not yield the covariance-dependent width constant for rectangles centered at the direct TWSF leading Gaussian estimator.

novelty_justification: The exact causal comparator is Shen (2026), whose Corollary 2 is pointwise and whose Section 6 deliberately reduces each prespecified fixed-horizon summary to a scalar before inference. The explicit \(H_n=1\) singleton-menu inclusion recovers that published result only as validation. The proposed theorem instead retains an \(H_n\)-vector, handles independently selected training from a fixed deterministic menu, and proves a feasible relative Gram rate for the actual fitted PCR, Riesz, terminal-block, and companion-Jacobian objects. Greenaway-McGrevy (2013) is the nearest architecture comparator: it derives asymptotic MSPE expressions for conventional direct and recursive panel-VAR forecasts and shows that their ranking depends on lag-order specification. Bhansali (1997) and Ing (2003) establish the broader direct-versus-plug-in MSPE comparison in autoregressive time series. Those predictive results motivate, but neither imply nor are sharpened by, the proposed causal selected-training score, Gaussian maximum and variance-share frontier, feasible Gram covariance, and simultaneous conditional-mean ribbon. Belloni et al. (2018) and Chernozhukov et al. (2015, 2017) provide the final orthogonal-score and Gaussian-comparison tools but do not supply this panel-specific linearization. The second theorem-level object, \(\rho_n\), aggregates heterogeneous lead-specific independent variance shares and gives the correct two-sided direct-complexity law alongside uniform bounded recursion; \(\nu_{\min,n}\) alone yields the simpler law only when the shares are uniformly comparable. No result in the verified TWSF, panel-VAR forecasting, autoregressive multistep forecasting, low-rank panel-inference, PCR, or simultaneous-band threads subsumes either the feasible growing-path theorem or this heterogeneous variance-share frontier.
